chapter: Building McShann's big band and blues records
title: Wichita, the Down Beat poll and the Chicago trip
summary: McShann built a base in Wichita; Down Beat voted them promising and he and Jay were brought to Chicago for six weeks.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Anyway, I found out about it after they had left town. But I wouldn't have gone, anyway. But anyway, then we -- McShann began to establish the name -- was (inaudible). He established a beachhead, a big beachhead, in Wichita. So we went down there. you may -- I remember having the urge heard some of the records, you know. McShann in his first thing.
Now, in the end of '38, we had been voted as the most promising new players on the horizon, or something.
Well, that's a result of Dave Dexter?

Probably. Anyway, and in the return we were -- Jay and I were brought to Chicago with a drummer who was supposed to have won, along there with George Barnes and Anita O'Day who also was supposed to have been the new stars for that time.
By the way, did you hear George Barnes died?
Of course you better erase that off. MR. DANCE: No, that's alright.
(Inaudible). And we stayed there for six weeks. We were supposed to go there for two weeks, and we stayed there six weeks.
